text:
amy_sales: quick sync — Acme wants us to stand up a POC using Private connectivity. They prefer peering if possible but asked about PrivateLink for client isolation. They need a short checklist (subnets, route tables, DNS, SGs) and any blockers for cross-account peering. timeline: POC by next Tue. cc @raj_solutions @luis_neteng

raj_solutions: summary: two main options — VPC Peering (simpler, lower cost) vs PrivateLink (managed endpoints, easier audit). main constraints: overlapping CIDRs, transitive routing, and customer security ops demanding endpoint/policy controls. ask: do they own the VPC in their account or want our VPC peered into theirs?

amy_sales: they own it. they asked if we can accept a peering connection from their account into our control-plane VPC. also asked about NAT / egress for model downloads.

luis_neteng: peering notes: cannot be transitive (no route propagation through a third VPC). ensure no CIDR overlap. if our control plane is 10.40.0.0/16 we need them to keep their ranges separate (eg 10.10.0.0/16). they should add route table entries like:
```
Destination: 10.40.0.0/16 -> Target: pcx-0abc12345
```
also: if they want to reach our management endpoints on 443, ensure security group on our side allows their VPC CIDR.

eng_kate: PrivateLink flow if they prefer: we create a Network Load Balancer in our VPC and publish an endpoint service (aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint-service-configuration). they then create an Interface VPC Endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce) in their subnets. advantage: fine-grained SG controls and no CIDR restrictions. downside: they must allow cross-account endpoint acceptance or we must auto-accept.

amy_sales: great. any specific subnet requirements? they have private subnets in multiple AZs.

luis_neteng: yes — for PrivateLink the customer needs interface endpoints in at least 2 AZs for HA. pick /24s per endpoint subnet (e.g., 10.10.100.0/24, 10.10.101.0/24). for peering, traffic uses existing route tables for private subnets. confirm their route tables include routes to the peering connection and no route propagation conflicts.

sre_maya: DNS: for PrivateLink we recommend enablePrivateDns=true so customer hostnames resolve to the interface endpoint. for peering, you need to manage DNS via conditional forwarding or shared resolver (Route 53 Resolver inbound/outbound rules) if they want private hostnames to map to our internal names. avoid split-brain on same hostnames.

raj_solutions: security checklist for POC:
- confirm non-overlapping CIDRs
- route table entries added for peering (example above)
- SG on our service side allows 443 from customer CIDR (or SG if they share)
- if NAT for model downloads is required, ensure outbound NAT gateway in our VPC or customer VPC as per architecture
- for PrivateLink: share service name, configure acceptance policy, and confirm endpoint ENI subnets and SGs

amy_sales: can we share a short artifact for the customer with exact steps and sample routes? they prefer copy/paste steps.

luis_neteng: I'll draft a minimal presales snippet they can use. include this route sample and a note about overlapping ranges. also add a short command for them to check peering status:
```
aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=requester-vpc-info.vpc-id,Values=vpc-xxxx
```

sre_maya: also include a reminder: peering does not support transitive routing; if they need to reach other AWS accounts or transit VPCs, recommend PrivateLink or Transit Gateway (TGW) as an alternative. TGW has extra cost and setup time.

deploy_bot: deployment-checklist created: poc-peering-1765123456.md (link: https://internal.docs/repo/poc-peering-1765123456) :white_check_mark:

amy_sales: perfect. timeline: can you have the snippet by EOD today? i'll send to Acme and loop their infra lead.

raj_solutions: yes — i'll post a short paste in this thread within a few hours. if Acme needs dedicated GPU pools we may need an additional network baseline for egress to monitoring endpoints — flagging now.

amy_sales: thanks all. i'll wait for the snippet then ping customer. :thumbsup:
